title: Hearing Arsenio Rodriguez in 1933
summary: Machito says Agabama and the Sexteto Bologna were far more advanced than Arsenio, who wrote music within his limits.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: All right. Fine. He came to New York- you and - later on you went with Agabama and from 1933 to 36 you were with Agabama.
Okay. With Agabama, you just worked in one place?
Okay. Had you heard of Arsenio Rodriguez yet, in 1933?
Okay. What did you hear about Arsenio?

Well, he is starting. Naturally, I mean I am telling you the truth. We were so far advanced, as a matter of fact, the Sexteto Bologna, with Latica Gutierrez, Bologna - there was a tres player we used to, they used to play fox trot, we used to play Spanish lyrics. They were too far advanced for Arsenio Rodriguez' ear. Arsenio Rodriguez was very talented because he create something that he could play. He knew his limitation and he never was above his limitation.
But in 1933, had he been playing son montuno yet?
That, that, that was his meat. That was the easiest thing because there was tonic and dominant, two or three chords that he was very acquainted with.
